subject: Intermittent large-packet drops on private link — routing vs security-group impact
messages:
From: Alex Gordon <alex.gordon@stormbridge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: support@stormbridge.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent packet drops to private deployment (large payloads)

Hi Ben —

We're seeing intermittent failures from our services to the Redwood Private deployment peering (StormBridge -> Redwood VPC). The symptom: requests with payloads larger than ~3.5KB occasionally fail with TCP retransmits and eventual timeouts. Smaller requests are fine. The problem started ~ 06/20 22:00 UTC and is still reproducible.

What we've observed:
- Packet capture attached (pcap-trace-20270621.pcap) shows a number of retransmit bursts where the sender is retransmitting 4–16KB chunks.
- Traceroute from our edge -> redwood edge looks stable; no apparent AS hops dropping.
- Firewall on our side is logging occasional "fragmentation needed" ICMPs but we don't see responses from the Redwood side.

This looks like large-packet reassembly/discard somewhere on the path or a PMTU problem. Could you confirm whether any intermediate security groups, NAT, or edge hosts are dropping large fragments or blocking ICMP type 3/4?

Attached: pcap and topology diagram showing the path (our edge -> StormBridge transit -> Redwood private edge).

Appreciate a quick triage — this is impacting a subset of customer flows.

Thanks,
Alex Gordon
Network Engineer | StormBridge
[attachment: pcap-trace-20270621.pcap]
[attachment: onprem-topology-20270621.svg]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gordon <alex.gordon@stormbridge.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent packet drops to private deployment (large payloads)

Alex —

Thanks for the pcap and topology, that helps. I'm looping in our infrastructure team (Dev) and the private-deploy lead (Evelyn) to help triage. Quick asks to narrow this down:

1) Can you confirm whether the DF (Don't Fragment) bit is being set by your sender when you see failures? If DF is set and ICMP type 3 code 4 is being blocked, PMTU discovery will fail.
2) Do you have any NAT appliances doing MSS clamping or TCP segmentation offload (GSO/GRO) changes in-line?
3) Can you paste the full output of tcpdump around a failing flow (timestamps, seq numbers) — the pcap helped but we may need a narrow capture with DF set on/off.

Dev — please check:
- Edge NAT/SG logs for any drops for connections from StormBridge at the times in the capture.
- Any recent changes to on-prem edge (iptables, conntrack limits, kernel offload settings) that might affect reassembly.

Evelyn — FYI; if this looks like a configuration mismatch we may need a short canary change at the private edge to allow ICMP 3/4 and perform a controlled test.

I'll coordinate comms with Alex.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Gordon <alex.gordon@stormbridge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: support@stormbridge.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent packet drops to private deployment (large payloads)

Ben —

Follow-up with a focused capture and a log excerpt. Two additional notes:

- We aren't setting DF intentionally; that said, our edge firewall (vendor: Netshell X200) enabled "segment coalesce" and GSO on the NICs last week during a maintenance window. When we forced GSO/GRO off on the host, the failures drop to near-zero in short tests. That suggests an offload/reassembly mismatch somewhere between our edge and the Redwood front-door or along the transit.
- The firewall also has an option "TCP MSS adjust" which was enabled as part of the maintenance; we can toggle that on demand.

Relevant log snippet (timestamps match pcap):
[2027-06-21T08:53:02Z] FW X200: packet dropped (frag-needed) dst=10.45.12.77 len=8192 proto=TCP
[2027-06-21T08:53:02Z] Host NIC: GSO: coalesce enabled

We can run a controlled test if Redwood can temporarily allow ICMP type 3 code 4 on the private-edge SG and/or disable any reassembly limits on your NAT.

Alex
Alex Gordon
Network Engineer | StormBridge

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alex Gordon <alex.gordon@stormbridge.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent packet drops to private deployment (large payloads)

Alex / Ben —

Thanks for the capture and the offload notes. Actionable plan from infra side:

1) I'll check the private-edge instances for any recent kernel offload changes (GSO/GRO/TCP segmentation offload). If offload is enabled mismatchedly on either side it can cause asymmetric packet chunking that middleboxes reject.
2) Can you run iperf3 from your edge to our private IP with these variants:
   - iperf3 -P 1 -M 1400 (force MSS 1400)
   - iperf3 -P 1 --set-mss 1400
   - iperf3 with DF bit set (we can help craft)
3) Please enable ICMP type 3 code 4 temporarily (we'll only require it for a 30m window) so PMTU discovery can succeed while we test. If enabling on SG is not acceptable we'll orchestrate a canary route via a jump-host to simulate.
4) I'll also look at conntrack and NAT session logs for signs of reassembly failures or conntrack entries flapping.

If tests show failures only when GSO/GRO are enabled on both ends, next step is to schedule a controlled NIC offload toggling across the edge pair during a low-impact window.

I'll post back after the first checks.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Team —

We need to escalate this to on-call network operations and schedule a controlled test tomorrow 09:00 PT. Planned steps:
- 09:00–09:15: Allow ICMP type 3 code 4 on the private-edge security group for StormBridge source prefixes.
- 09:15–09:45: Run coordinated iperf3 tests (Dev and Alex) with and without NIC offload / MSS adjustments.
- 09:45–10:15: Review pcap/edge logs and revert SG change.

Rishi, please prepare firewall/NAT session logs and a short script to toggle GSO/GRO on the private-edge instances. Marissa, loop in account exec for StormBridge and set expectations — keep the change window short and notify customers.

Alex — thanks for quick triage so far. We'll keep the SG change limited and monitor for any side-effects. If the test reproduces the failure we will coordinate a permanent mitigation (disable offload at edge, or adjust MSS handling).

Action items:
- Dev: confirm edge kernel offload settings (ETA 2h)
- Rishi: gather conntrack/NAT logs for the 08:50–09:00 UTC window (ETA 3h)
- Ben/Marissa: notify StormBridge of the 09:00 PT test window (Ben to confirm)

I'll update this thread after the test.

Evelyn Hart
